answer: To resist sybils, each new identity posts a refundable bond that unlocks only after a rotating peer bridge of established graders has countersigned its work. Fresh accounts get a velvet privilege cap: they may submit answers, but cannot grade or vote until N independent panels attest them over several epochs. Near-duplicate clusters slash every account in the set and quarantine their attestations. A comet decay shrinks unused reputation each epoch, so attackers cannot bank cheap identities and later flood the network. Cohort cost grows with bond size and panel wait, not just with minted keys.
